html:
The Awabakal are an Aboriginal Australian people of the New South Wales coast between the Hunter River and the Gosford region, including today's Newcastle and Lake Macquarie. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land of beaches, lakes and the Watagan Mountains gave fish, shellfish and game. A convict settlement opened at Newcastle in 1804 to dig coal, one of the first coal mines in Australia.

The Awabakal language is one of the best recorded of early New South Wales. From 1825 the missionary Lancelot Threlkeld ran a mission at Lake Macquarie and worked with the Awabakal man Biraban to write a grammar of the language and translate parts of the Bible into it. Neighbours on the map include the Worimi, the Guringai and the Wonnarua. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
